headline: Approved September minutes; discussed invasive bittersweet cleanup, Ethan Tapper event, and possible tree removal on Cypress Street.
summary: The group discussed an October 24 event with author Ethan Tapper and plans for bittersweet cleanup. It also discussed fundraising, school projects, State House trees, and a resident's concern about possible tree removal on Cypress Street for proposed sidewalks. The only recorded vote approved the September 22, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Approved the September 22, 2026 minutes as written by unanimous voice vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. Regan moved the approval of the September 22, 2026, minutes as written. Ms. Corell seconded the motion. The motion passed by unanimous voice vote.

Conservation Commission Tree Sub-Committee 1 
Meeting Minutes  2 
October 22, 2026 @ 8:00 AM - DRAFT 3 
Council Chambers 4 
37 Green Street, Concord, NH 5 
 6 
In Attendance:  7 
Subcommittee Members: Tom Daigle (Chair), Craig Tufts (Vice Chair), Elizabeth Corell, John Regan, Steve Winnett, Rick 8 
Chormann, Peter Breu  9 
Absent:  Stacey Brown, Ted Diers, Brooke Gauthier 10 
Guests: Liz McKinley, DNCR; Jo Russavage, UNH Cooperative Extension 11 
Staff: Beth Fenstermacher, Director of Special Projects and Strategic Initiatives of Community Development 12 
Chair Daigle called the meeting to order at 8:03 A.M.   13 
1. Adoption of September 22, 2026 Minutes 14 
Mr. Regan moved the approval of the September 22, 2026, minutes as written. Ms. Corell seconded the motion. The 15 
motion passed by unanimous voice vote.  16 
2. October 24th Ethan Tapper event 17 
Ms. Russavage provided an update on the planning for the October 24th event with forester and author Ethan Tapper. 18 
She reported that the morning walk has additional space available if the Tree Subcommittee would like to extend the 19 
invitation. Ms. Fenstermacher will send the link to the Conservation Commission. Ms. Russavage reported that 33 people 20 
have purchased tickets for the afternoon event at the Forest Society.  21 
3. Committee Procedures 22 
Ms. Fenstermacher reported that the Tree Subcommittee will be receiving an email from the City Clerks office with 23 
copies of the City’s Code of Ethics, and a request to sign an oath, as other City Boards and Committee members as 24 
required to do. She reported that she emailed members a memo from the City Solicitor about the RSA 91-A right to know 25 
requirements. Further, she will request that the Conservation Commission adopt a formal organizing policy to establish 26 
term limits, same as other Boards and Committees in the City.  27 
4. Bob Pollock Tree Tour Policy 28 
Chair Daigle will organize a meeting with Bob Pollock, Ms. Gauthier, and Ms. Fenstermacher to discuss a plan for moving 29 
forward. Ms. Corell asked if this subcommittee will look at how to fundraise for Mr. Pollocks stipend. Mr. Winnett 30 
indicated that he would like to be involved and lead tours. 31 
5. Follow up 32 
a. Invasive Vines and Farmers Market 33 
Mr. Winnett reported that he would like to form a group of interested volunteers to go out every weekend to focus 34 
on bittersweet clean-up in addition to a few, bigger educational events. Ms. Russavage suggested scheduling the 35 
educational events around key dates in the invasive removal calendar. Mr. Winnett reported that the Merrimack 36 
River Watershed Council (MRWC) is hosting an invasives removal event on private property along the Contoocook 37

River on October 25th.  The subcommittee discussed strengthening the relationship with MRWC to collaborate on 1 
future events. Mr. Winnett will invite Mark Feigl from MRWC to the next meeting. 2 
b. Opportunities to collaborate 3 
Chair Daigle will be attending an upcoming Chamber event with a goal to continue to grow the relationship with 4 
the Chamber. Mr. Winnett reported that he has spoken to Rundlett Middle School and Concord High School about 5 
school projects with students to remove invasives.  6 
UNH Cooperative Extension and the State continue to be great partners that the subcommittee would like to 7 
continue working with. 8 
c. Fundraising/Grant opportunities 9 
Ms. McKinley reported that the trees awarded to Christ McAuliffe School will be planted next spring. The 10 
Schoolyard Canopy Enhancement program will be offered again next year. 11 
Mr. Regan reported that Unitil donated $150 to the City. Mr. Regan suggested partnering with a non-profit/501c3 12 
organization to help fundraise.  Chair Daigle suggested that the subcommittee could draft a 1-pager about the 13 
fundraising efforts, and perhaps be used to seek corporate sponsorships. 14 
6. New Business 15 
a. State House Trees – Ms. McKinley reported that new Cherry trees were planted and sugar maples gifted by Canada 16 
will be planted soon. 17 
b. Public comments – Chris Moore, a resident of Cypress Street asked to provide comments to the subcommittee. He 18 
reported that the City is proposing sidewalks on Cypress Street, which could result in the removal of trees. This 19 
work is related to the bus route for the new Middle School.  Chair Daigle stated the Tree Subcommittee does not 20 
have any jurisdiction over this matter. Mr. Moore acknowledged, but wanted to make the Tree SC aware.  21 
7. Next Meeting Date 22 
Thursday, November 19, 2026 at 8 a.m. 23 
A motion to adjourn was made by Ms. Corell. The motion was seconded by Mr. Regan. The motion passed by unanimous 24 
voice vote.  25 
Meeting adjourned at 9:07 A.M. 26
